q: How long is a regulation badminton court?
hint: For scale: a tennis court is about {24 m} long.
card: A shuttlecock’s feathers create so much drag that it slows sharply over distance, even after the fastest smashes.
clue: A volleyball court is {18 m} long.

q: How wide is the hole on a golf green?
hint: For scale: a golf ball is about {4.3 cm} across.
card: The size became the official standard in 1891, based on a hole-cutting tool used at Musselburgh in Scotland since 1829.
clue: A soda can is about {6.6 cm} across.

q: How far is the NBA three-point line from the basket at the top of the arc?
hint: For scale: a basketball rim is {3.05 m} off the floor.
card: The NBA only adopted the three-point shot in 1979, more than three decades after the league was founded.
clue: The free-throw line is about {4.6 m} from the backboard.

q: In what year were the first Wimbledon tennis championships played?
hint: For scale: Queen Victoria came to the throne in 1837.
card: The first tournament had only a men’s singles event, with 22 players; women did not compete until 1884.
clue: The American Civil War ended in 1865.

q: How many feathers make up a standard feathered badminton shuttlecock?
hint: For scale: a spider has 8 legs.
card: The feathers usually come from geese or ducks, and the best shuttles take them all from the same wing so the shuttle spins evenly.
clue: There are 12 months in a year.

q: What is the most clubs a golfer is allowed to carry in a round under the official rules?
hint: For scale: a week has 7 days.
card: Carrying too many clubs costs a two-stroke penalty for each hole where the rule was broken, up to four strokes in a round.
clue: There are 12 months in a year.

q: How heavy is the discus thrown by men in Olympic competition?
hint: For scale: a soccer ball weighs about {0.43 kg}.
card: Discus throwing was part of the ancient Greek pentathlon, and the sport returned at the first modern Olympics in 1896.
clue: A full {1 L} bottle of water weighs about {1 kg}.

q: How many episodes of The Sopranos were made?
hint: For scale: a typical US network sitcom season had about 22 episodes.
card: The series famously ends with a sudden cut to black, and many viewers at first thought their cable had gone out.
clue: Game of Thrones ran for 73 episodes.

q: How long is The Wizard of Oz (1939)?
hint: For scale: a typical TV sitcom episode runs about 22 minutes.
card: In L. Frank Baum’s book the magic slippers are silver; the film made them ruby red to show off its Technicolor.
clue: Disney’s Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937) runs about 83 minutes.

q: In what year was Steven Spielberg’s E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial released?
hint: For scale: the first Moon landing was in 1969.
card: E.T. passed Star Wars to become the highest-grossing film of its time, a record it held until Jurassic Park.
clue: Jaws came out in 1975.

q: How many seasons of M*A*S*H were made?
hint: For scale: Seinfeld ran for 9 seasons.
card: The show ran several times longer than the Korean War it was set in, and its 1983 finale drew about 106 million US viewers.
clue: Friends ran for 10 seasons.

q: How many Oscars did Ben-Hur (1959) win?
hint: For scale: Casablanca won 3 Oscars.
card: Its chariot race sequence alone took about five weeks to film on one of the largest sets ever built.
clue: The Godfather Part II won 6 Oscars.

q: In what year did Sesame Street first air?
hint: For scale: the Korean War ended in 1953.
card: Big Bird is played from inside the costume, with the performer holding one arm up to work the head the whole time.
clue: John F. Kennedy became US president in 1961.

q: How many episodes of Stranger Things were made in total?
hint: For scale: a typical US network sitcom season had about 22 episodes.
card: The show is set in the fictional town of Hawkins, Indiana, beginning in November 1983.
clue: The Wire ran for 60 episodes.

q: In what year did Elvis Presley release “Heartbreak Hotel”?
hint: For scale: World War II ended in 1945.
card: It became his first million-selling record and his first No. 1 hit in the United States.
clue: The Korean War began in 1950.

q: On a standard 88-key piano, how many keys are black?
hint: For scale: a guitar has 6 strings.
card: The black keys follow a repeating pattern of two and three, which is how pianists find their place without looking.
clue: A deck of playing cards has 26 red cards.

q: In what year did Michael Jackson first perform the moonwalk on television?
hint: For scale: the Beatles split up in 1970.
card: He debuted it during “Billie Jean” on the Motown 25 TV special, wearing his single sequined glove.
clue: Space Invaders hit arcades in 1978.

q: In what year did Apple open the iTunes Store for selling music?
hint: For scale: Windows 95 came out in 1995.
card: Songs cost 99 cents each at launch, and the store sold over a million in its first week.
clue: Google was founded in 1998.

q: In what year did ABBA win the Eurovision Song Contest with “Waterloo”?
hint: For scale: the Berlin Wall went up in 1961.
card: “Waterloo” was sung in English, a choice that helped turn a Swedish pop group into a worldwide act.
clue: The first Moon landing was in 1969.

q: How long is Led Zeppelin’s “Stairway to Heaven,” in seconds?
hint: For scale: a typical pop single lasts about 210 seconds.
card: It was never released as a single in the US, yet it became one of the most requested songs on American FM radio.
clue: Queen’s “Bohemian Rhapsody” runs about 355 seconds.

q: How many finger and thumb holes does a standard recorder have?
hint: For scale: a trumpet has 3 valves.
card: Recorders were popular in Renaissance and Baroque Europe long before they became a staple of school music classes.
clue: A guitar has 6 strings.

q: In how many ways can two eight-stud LEGO bricks of the same color be snapped together?
hint: For scale: a die has 6 faces.
card: LEGO bricks made today still fit bricks made in 1958, when the patent for the modern stud-and-tube design was filed.
clue: There are 12 months in a year.

q: How many squares wide is the playing field in standard Tetris?
hint: For scale: a tic-tac-toe grid is 3 squares wide.
card: Alexey Pajitnov wrote it on a Soviet computer in Moscow; the name blends tetra, Greek for four, with tennis, his favorite sport.
clue: A chessboard is 8 squares wide.

q: How many points is the letter Q worth in English-language Scrabble?
hint: For scale: the letter E is worth just 1 point.
card: Only one Q comes in an English set, and there are just a handful of common words that use it without a U, such as “qi”.
clue: The letter K is worth 5 points.

q: How many rooms are in the mansion on the classic Clue (Cluedo) game board?
hint: For scale: a hand has 5 fingers.
card: The game was invented in England during World War II by Anthony Pratt, a musician who played at murder-mystery parties.
clue: There are 12 months in a year.

q: In what year did Nintendo release the Wii?
hint: For scale: the first PlayStation launched in 1994.
card: Its motion-sensing remote got so many people swinging that wrist straps became a must, after reports of remotes flying into TV screens.
clue: The PlayStation 2 launched in 2000.

q: How many points is a Yahtzee (five of a kind) worth the first time you score one?
hint: For scale: a full house scores 25 points.
card: The game was first sold as “The Yacht Game,” named after the yacht where a Canadian couple invented it.
clue: A large straight scores 40 points.

q: In what year did Parker Brothers first publish Monopoly?
hint: For scale: the Model T Ford went on sale in 1908.
card: The game grew out of The Landlord’s Game, designed by Lizzie Magie in 1904 to show the problems with land monopolies.
clue: The first Academy Awards were handed out in 1929.

q: How tall is the dome of St. Peter’s Basilica in Vatican City, to the top of its cross?
hint: For scale: a 10-story building is about {30 m} tall.
card: Michelangelo designed the dome but died before it was finished; it was completed in 1590.
clue: London’s St Paul’s Cathedral rises about {111 m}.

q: How tall is the Empire State Building, to the tip of its antenna?
hint: For scale: a 10-story building is about {30 m} tall.
card: Its mast was first designed as a mooring point for airships, an idea dropped after strong winds made it impractical.
clue: Taipei 101 rises about {508 m}.

q: How tall is India’s Statue of Unity, the world’s tallest statue?
hint: For scale: a 10-story building is about {30 m} tall.
card: It depicts Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, a leader of Indian independence, and opened in 2018.
clue: London’s Big Ben clock tower is about {96 m} tall.

q: How tall is Cinderella Castle at Walt Disney World, measured from water level?
hint: For scale: a typical two-story house is about {8 m} tall.
card: Builders used forced perspective, shrinking the upper stones and windows so the castle looks taller than it is.
clue: The Statue of Liberty, from its base to the torch, is about {46 m} tall.

q: How tall is the Shanghai Tower, China’s tallest building?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower is about {330 m} tall.
card: Its outer glass skin twists about 120 degrees as it rises, which helps it shrug off typhoon winds.
clue: Dubai’s Burj Khalifa is about {828 m} tall.

q: In what year did Walt Disney World open in Florida?
hint: For scale: Disney’s Snow White came out in 1937.
card: Walt Disney died in 1966, five years before it opened, so his brother Roy saw the project through.
clue: Apple was founded in 1976.

q: How long was each side of the Great Pyramid of Giza’s base when it was built?
hint: For scale: a soccer field is about {105 m} long.
card: The four sides line up with north, south, east and west to within a small fraction of a degree.
clue: The Titanic was about {269 m} long.

q: In what year was the James Webb Space Telescope launched?
hint: For scale: the Space Shuttle made its last flight in 2011.
card: It launched on Christmas Day and works about {1,500,000 km} from Earth, far beyond the Moon.
clue: The Rosetta probe landed a craft on a comet in 2014.

q: In what year was the planet Neptune discovered?
hint: For scale: Uranus was discovered in 1781.
card: It was found by math first: astronomers predicted its position from wobbles in Uranus’s orbit, and it was spotted almost exactly there.
clue: Queen Victoria came to the throne in 1837.

q: How many Earth years go by while Uranus circles the Sun once?
hint: For scale: Saturn takes about 29 years.
card: Uranus is tipped on its side, so each pole gets about 42 years of sunlight followed by 42 years of darkness.
clue: Neptune takes about 165 years.

q: What is the diameter of Pluto?
hint: For scale: Earth is about {12,742 km} across.
card: Pluto is smaller than Earth’s Moon, and its largest moon, Charon, is about half Pluto’s width.
clue: The Moon is about {3,474 km} across.

q: How fast does Earth’s surface move at the equator because of the planet’s spin?
hint: For scale: a passenger jet cruises at about {900 km/h}.
card: You don’t feel it because the ground, the air and you all move together at the same steady speed.
clue: Concorde cruised at about {2,180 km/h}.

q: How many minutes does the International Space Station take to circle Earth once?
hint: For scale: a typical TV sitcom episode runs about 22 minutes.
card: That means astronauts aboard see about 16 sunrises and 16 sunsets every day.
clue: A feature film often runs about 120 minutes.

q: In what year did Galileo discover Jupiter’s four largest moons?
hint: For scale: Shakespeare was born in 1564.
card: They were the first moons found orbiting another planet, which helped convince people that not everything circles Earth.
clue: The Mayflower reached America in 1620.

q: How many toes does an ostrich have on each foot?
hint: For scale: a human foot has 5 toes.
card: Most birds have four toes on each foot, so the ostrich stands out.
clue: A chicken has 4 toes on each foot.

q: How many chromosomes are in a typical dog body cell?
hint: For scale: a fruit fly cell has 8 chromosomes.
card: Wolves also have 78, one reason dogs and wolves can still interbreed.
clue: A chimpanzee cell has 48 chromosomes.

q: How many days does a horse’s pregnancy usually last?
hint: For scale: a dog’s pregnancy lasts about 63 days.
card: A newborn foal can usually stand and walk within a short time of being born.
clue: A human pregnancy lasts about 280 days.

q: How much blood is in a typical adult human body?
hint: For scale: a large soda bottle holds {2 L}.
card: Red blood cells make up nearly half of that volume.
clue: A gallon jug of milk holds about {3.8 L}.

q: What is the normal human body temperature?
hint: For scale: water boils at {100 °C}.
card: The figure dates to German doctor Carl Wunderlich’s work in the 1860s; newer studies find many people run slightly cooler.
clue: A very hot summer day can reach about {45 °C}.

q: How many legs does a pill bug (roly-poly) have?
hint: For scale: an insect has 6 legs.
card: Pill bugs are not insects but crustaceans, more closely related to shrimp and crabs.
clue: A lobster has 10 legs.

q: How many living species of elephant do scientists recognize?
hint: For scale: there are 8 living species of bear.
card: The African forest elephant was long treated as part of the African bush elephant species, until DNA studies showed they are distinct.
clue: There are 5 living species of rhinoceros.

q: In what year was the first US transcontinental railroad completed?
hint: For scale: the California Gold Rush began in 1848.
card: The line was finished with a ceremonial golden spike at Promontory Summit, Utah, cutting a cross-country trip from months to about a week.
clue: Abraham Lincoln became US president in 1861.

q: In what year did Hawaii become a US state?
hint: For scale: World War II ended in 1945.
card: It is the only US state made up entirely of islands, and the only one outside North America.
clue: The Korean War ended in 1953.

q: In what year was the US Constitution signed?
hint: For scale: the Boston Tea Party happened in 1773.
card: It is the oldest written national constitution still in use, and it fits on just four sheets of parchment.
clue: The US Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776.

q: How tall was Abraham Lincoln?
hint: For scale: a basketball rim is {3.05 m} off the floor.
card: He remains the tallest US president, and his famous stovepipe hat made him look taller still.
clue: Napoleon was about {1.69 m} tall.

q: How long was the Oregon Trail, the wagon route to the American West?
hint: For scale: New York to Chicago is about {1,150 km} in a straight line.
card: Many emigrants walked the whole way beside their wagons, covering about {24 km} on a good day.
clue: Route 66 ran about {3,940 km}.

q: How many passengers did the Mayflower carry to America in 1620?
hint: For scale: a school classroom holds about 30 students.
card: A baby named Oceanus Hopkins was born at sea during the crossing.
clue: A Boeing 737 often carries about 150 passengers.

q: How many years did it take to carve Mount Rushmore?
hint: For scale: a US president’s term is 4 years.
card: About 90% of the mountain was carved with dynamite, then finished by hand.
clue: The US took 10 years to build the Panama Canal.

q: How much did the original 2007 iPhone weigh?
hint: For scale: a can of soda weighs about {0.37 kg}.
card: It had no app store at launch; Apple opened the App Store a year later.
clue: A large apple weighs about {0.2 kg}.

q: In what year did the Ford Mustang go on sale?
hint: For scale: World War II ended in 1945.
card: It went on sale in April, and Ford sold about 400,000 in its first year, far more than it had expected.
clue: Elvis Presley was drafted into the US Army in 1958.

q: How long is the Boeing 747-8, the longest version of the jumbo jet?
hint: For scale: a blue whale can be about {30 m} long.
card: The 747’s famous hump was designed so the nose could swing up for loading cargo.
clue: The Statue of Liberty, ground to torch, is about {93 m} tall.

q: In what year was the Magnavox Odyssey, the first home video game console, released?
hint: For scale: the first nationwide US color TV broadcast was in 1954.
card: It had no sound or color; players taped plastic overlays onto their TV screens to make the games look like tennis or hockey.
clue: The Berlin Wall went up in 1961.

q: How heavy is NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover?
hint: For scale: an adult male African elephant weighs about {6,000 kg}.
card: It carried a small helicopter, Ingenuity, which made the first powered flight on another planet in 2021.
clue: A small car weighs about {1,300 kg}.

q: How long is the Ever Given, the container ship that blocked the Suez Canal in 2021?
hint: For scale: a soccer field is about {105 m} long.
card: It stayed stuck for six days, holding up hundreds of ships waiting to pass.
clue: The Titanic was about {269 m} long.

q: How many cylinders does the Bugatti Veyron’s engine have?
hint: For scale: most family cars have 4 cylinders.
card: Its engine is arranged as two V8s joined together, an unusual layout called a W16.
clue: A Lamborghini Aventador has 12 cylinders.

q: How long is a US dollar bill?
hint: For scale: a credit card is about {8.6 cm} long.
card: US paper money is not really paper: it is mostly cotton with some linen, which is why it survives the wash.
clue: A standard pencil is about {19 cm} long.

q: How long is one nautical mile?
hint: For scale: a lap of a running track is {0.4 km}.
card: A nautical mile was originally based on one minute of latitude, which is why sailors and pilots still use it.
clue: A regular mile is about {1.61 km}.

q: How much does a US gallon of water weigh?
hint: For scale: a {1 L} bottle of water weighs about {1 kg}.
card: A US gallon is smaller than the imperial gallon once used in Britain, which holds about 20% more.
clue: A house cat weighs about {4.5 kg}.

q: How many countries share a land border with Germany?
hint: For scale: the United States borders 2 countries.
card: Its neighbors range from big countries like France and Poland to tiny Luxembourg.
clue: Brazil borders 10 countries.

q: How many letters are in the Greek alphabet?
hint: For scale: the Hawaiian alphabet has 13 letters.
card: The word “alphabet” itself comes from its first two letters, alpha and beta.
clue: The Russian alphabet has 33 letters.

q: How many US teaspoons fill one US cup?
hint: For scale: there are 7 days in a week.
card: Three teaspoons make a tablespoon, and 16 tablespoons make a cup.
clue: There are 24 hours in a day.

q: How tall is a standard interior door in a US home?
hint: For scale: a basketball rim is {3.05 m} off the floor.
card: US door sizes are set in inches, so the standard height is a round 80 inches.
clue: An average American man is about {1.75 m} tall.
